target.title: fix(slack): react action rejects emoji glyphs; member-info userId affordance unclear
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two message-tool parameter affordances invite a shape the Slack backend rejects at runtime.

1. The `react`/`reactions` actions accept an `emoji` param with no description, so models pass a raw Unicode glyph (for example "✅"). Slack's `reactions.add` only accepts shortcode names (for example "white_check_mark"), so the call fails:

   ```
   [tools] message failed: An API error occurred: invalid_name raw_params={"action":"react","messageId":"1783075043.703069","emoji":"✅"}
   ```

2. The `member-info` action has no target mode (`MESSAGE_ACTION_TARGET_MODE["member-info"] = "none"`), so passing the universal `target` param throws:

   ```
   [tools] message failed: Action member-info does not accept a target. raw_params={"action":"member-info","channel":"slack","target":"channel:...", ...}
   ```

   `member-info` requires `userId` directly, but that field had no description steering models away from `target`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deterministic normalization and clearer schema descriptions at the tool boundary fix this for every call, instead of relying on prompt-side nagging that models will still occasionally miss.

While tracing the react path, a second, independent implementation of the same glyph-to-shortname mapping already existed in `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts` (`toSlackEmojiName` / `UNICODE_TO_SLACK`), used only for the agent's own internal ack/progress reactions. The model-facing `react` action never went through it, since it calls `reactSlackMessage` directly. Rather than adding a third copy, the mapping was consolidated into the one function both paths already share (`normalizeEmoji`, now exported as `normalizeSlackEmojiName` from `extensions/slack/src/actions.ts`, the layer that owns the actual `reactions.add`/`reactions.remove` calls), and `dispatch.ts` was updated to call the shared export instead of keeping its own copy.

## User Impact

- Slack `react`/`reactions` calls now work when the model passes a raw emoji glyph, a `:shortname:`, or a plain shortname. Unknown glyphs still pass through unchanged (no behavior change for that case).
- The `react` action's `emoji` param description now says a Slack emoji shortcode name is expected, not the emoji character. This is scoped to the Slack channel only (via the existing per-channel schema contribution seam in `extensions/slack/src/message-tool-api.ts`), so other channels' `emoji` param wording is untouched.
- The generic `userId` param description (used by `member-info` and moderation/participant actions) now states it is taken directly and that `target` is not accepted for those actions.
- One pre-existing test (`extensions/slack/src/monitor.tool-result.test.ts`) asserted the old, buggy behavior for the "status reactions disabled" ack-reaction path (a raw "eyes" glyph reaching the mocked Slack client unmapped). That path shares the same underlying function, so it is fixed as a side effect; the test now asserts the corrected value, consistent with its three sibling tests that already expected the mapped shortname.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/slack-message-tool-param-affordances`, based on synced `main` (`a308e3b834`).

Red/green proof:
- `extensions/slack/src/actions.reactions.test.ts`: added 6 cases (glyph, colon-wrapped shortname, plain shortname, unmapped glyph, skin-tone variant, variation-selector variant). All failed for the expected reason (3 glyph-mapping cases) before the fix, all 11 pass after.
- `extensions/slack/src/message-tools.test.ts`: added 2 cases asserting the `react`/`reactions` schema contribution's `emoji` description and its absence when reactions are disabled. Failed with "Missing schema property emoji" before the fix, all 12 pass after.
- `src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts`: added 1 case asserting the generic `userId` description mentions `member-info` and that `target` is not accepted. Failed with `undefined` description before the fix, all 117 pass after.
- Full Slack extension suite (`pnpm test extensions/slack`): 106 files / 1467 tests pass, including the one pre-existing test updated above.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `pnpm build`: clean (see PR comment/local run for output).

Before/after for the primary error:

```
raw_params={"action":"react","messageId":"1783075043.703069","emoji":"✅"}
# before: name sent to Slack = "✅" -> invalid_name
# after:  name sent to Slack = "white_check_mark" -> accepted
```

## Left Out (Ambiguous)

`member-info` also declared no target mode, and `target: "user:<id>"` could in principle translate to `userId`. This was deliberately left out: `member-info` needs channel-specific additional context on some channels (Discord's handler also requires `guildId`, not just a user id), and `MessageActionTargetMode` is a shared enum (`"to" | "channelId" | "none"`) consumed by every other action's target handling in `src/infra/outbound/message-action-spec.ts` and `channel-target.ts`. Adding a `"userId"` mode would touch that shared contract for a translation that is not obviously unambiguous across channels, so only the description-based steering was implemented.
